acceptance_condition: A structured extraction with the key definitions and at least 4 formal results across the two papers, each with file path + PDF page marker, plus a clearly labeled inferential mapping to communication-protocol synthesis/aggregation stages.
rationale: These papers provide the formal vocabulary for the causal model's synthesis and aggregation components (D3): Dung gives principled conflict resolution over attack graphs; CRDTs characterize when shared-state merging is safe and what invariants an open transcript would need.
text: Extract from papers/text/dung-1995-argumentation.txt and papers/text/shapiro-et-al-2011-crdts.txt: (a) from Dung, the formal apparatus relevant to synthesizing conflicting claims — argumentation frameworks, attack relations, admissible/grounded/preferred extensions — with precise definitions and the key theorems (e.g., existence/uniqueness of grounded extension); (b) from Shapiro et al., the CRDT conditions under which concurrent updates converge without coordination (commutativity/idempotency, monotonic semilattice joins), and the distinction between state-based and operation-based replication; (c) an assessment, labeled as the investigator's inference, of how each formalism could model the synthesis stage of staged retrieval-mediated Q/A (conflict resolution among agent answers) versus an open shared transcript (convergent replicated state). Record definitions/results with file path and explicit `===== PDF PAGE N =====` markers.
